notes.title: Version 1.52
notes.content:
Hey y'all! My desire with this game is to make sure that Rank 20 matches are hard enough that the people in my discord can't beat them (to create headroom) and to make sure that Rank 1 was easy enough that no one I can find is unable to beat those. This patch is yet another in that search. I improved the code a lot RE: how enemies are spawned so I think you should be seeing a lot more consistent results now. Also, omni-golems never did their job and they were kind of hacky anyway.

[b]ENJOY![/b]

[h1]Patch Notes[/h1]
Heads up! The hardest parts of this game just got harder. Ranks 15-20 now have more units per enemy spawn, and some Omni-Mob units have their stats changed a bit. Also though, the easiest ranks should be even *easier*! So you may have to mess around and pick a new difficulty to find the right one for you. Let us know where you seem to have a good, balanced battle!
- Omni-Golems removed from the game!
- Instead, after turn 12 the enemy reinforcements will start coming in every 2 turns instead of every 3 turns.
- Golden Reapers now have 9 attack, up from 7
- Omni Drill Sgts. now have 12 health, up from 10
- Lich Death Bolt damage 3=>4
- Fixed an Alcove Prefex bug with the sniper
- Summon Seedling now has a 2 turn cooldown. Take care of your seedlings!
- Seedlings and Fanatics (both player versions and summoned versions) attack damage 3=>2. It's good enough that your summons can absorb attacks, collect gems and rescue units!
- There were a couple of bugs with how enemies were spawning around castles before. The code for castle-guard-mobs has been changed so it's a lot more clear now, and works a lot more consistently. This means there's now ZERO castle guard-friends at rank 1, and SIX at rank 20.

notes.title: GWT gets a new faction: the Alcove Prefex
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38602491/6ec3a5a05fcf85f95392cc5daef40585aba2aec7.jpg[/img]

Introducing the ALCOVE PREFEX, Gem Wizards Tactics' fifth faction!

Because of how complex this game is, in terms of units, abilities, buffs and whatnot, and how original each faction is from each other, each "faction" is kind of huge. It's more like a new Starcraft faction than it is like a new Advance Wars faction, that's for sure.

So when we launched with three factions, I thought that was a pretty decent amount of complexity for the game (same number as Starcraft!). But then we added the NEVERENDING PARTY to the game, and I was like, okay, now we have one MORE faction than Starcraft - that definitely ought to be enough.

Development was starting to wind down a few months ago, after the addition of the map editor. And it was just then that our head tester Reschiiv (Emil Klarsson) approached me about designing a faction for the game! :O

So now, here you have it, the first Gem Wizards Tactics faction by a guest designer! Reschiiv did an amazing job both designing and then implementing this faction, and I can't thank him enough for his efforts. I wrote a song and did all the art and it was pretty much ready to go.

This is a very complex faction, for experienced players, I think. I've played with it a little bit and I can see the potential for some really amazing combos. Here's some of the neat stuff this faction can do:

- Summon two TWIN robots. If one robot dies, the other EXPLODES!
- Set up two warp pods that swap the places of two units standing on them
- HACK the terrain, copying large areas of tiles and terrain and swapping them with another position
- HACK other units and get them fighting for your team
- It has lasers and tanks and a WARMECH!

Oh, and I guess I haven't mentioned it, but we're not charging anything for this faction, or any of the additions to this game. It's FREE! So you have no excuse but to go check it out, and let us know what you think!

I'm getting started on a new project, so I don't expect there to be a lot in the way of new Gem Wizards Tactics updates over the next few months. That said, the game will be hitting other platforms soon, so stay tuned for that.

Enjoy!

notes.title: GWT Gets a MAP EDITOR!
notes.content:
[h2]Hello everyone! [/h2]

Today is a historic day in [i]Gem Wizards Tactics[/i] history: the game officially has a [b]MAP EDITOR[/b]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38602491/e7c24cab678c4713ab7153c628cdd8c7332a3d36.png[/img]

You can now create, save, and load [i]Gem Wizards Tactics[/i] maps, with whatever units, terrain or other stuff you might want to put in there. It also has some other cool features which might help you do whatever you're looking to do:

- Turn on/off randomized combat (may be useful for, say, a puzzle map)
- Turn on/off fog of war
- Change the number of flags required to win
- Add a MISSION TIMER - you need to win before X turns, or you lose.

You can save your map to a .MAP file also so you can share it with friends!

This should be a really fun thing to play with. It hasn't gotten a ton of testing yet, but it definitely works. Looking forward to hearing what you think, and what you'd like to see in the map editor. Send us your creations!

I should give credit and mention that this map editor was created by Brett Lowey of BrainGoodGames - amazing work Brett! 

If you missed it, we also got controller support in the last month, so make sure to check that out too!

Thanks everyone. And there is actually a LOT more cool, exciting stuff on the way for this game, so stay tuned!

- Keith

notes.title: Version 1.43 Patch Notes
notes.content:
Version 1.43
This is another version that includes a LOT of polish, bug-fixing, and balancing. We've also reverted somewhat on a big change that was in 1.42, so heads up that Gem Power is BACK! Overall I've been playtesting a lot and really enjoying the game, but please come by the Discord or Steam Forums if you have any thoughts!

- Scorch has been a bit too harsh of a penalty to movement. Each turn, Scorch tiles have a 40% chance to turn back into grass.
- Reverted some of the recent changes to how abilities work: it now is a bit of a hybrid of the way the game has worked for a long time, and the new cooldown ideas. Gem Power is brought back: some abilities, most particularly your Wizard's, need Gem Power to cast. Most abilities do not have cooldowns, but a handful do.
- Gems no longer heal you.
- Summon Amp, Rocket Jump, Wildfire, Chill Step, and Siege Attack have 2 turn CDs.
- Returned to the normal pre 1.42 generation of Gems on a map
- Minor change to how fog works: once you reveal a unit, you permanently see them.
- Finally fixed a couple of issues with Castle Guards. They should wake up when pushed or bounced now.
- Fog of War vision radius increased from 3 => 4
- New fog artwork completely covers tiles.
- Reap now deals 0 damage to adjacent units unless there are 3 or more adjacent enemies, in which case it deals 2 damage to all adjacent enemies.
- Reap no longer reaps Deathberry Bushes.
- Splashmaster's Water Tank buffs brought back (and he lost his Aquatic buff!)
- Knight Charge no longer has a cooldown.
- Knight now needs CARROTS to do his Charge ability. Gain 1 Carrot for ending your turn on a grass tile.
- Roadie's PULL ability is now HEAVE: Bounce an adjacent unit backwards over your head 3 tiles.
- Roadie no longer has summon amp. Instead, SHE has the Amplify ability.
- Roadie AP 4=>3
- Roadie Attack 3=>2
- Amplify ONLY targets adjacent friendly units, and doesn't bump adjacent units.
- A system wide rule that didn't really matter until now: it used to be that secondary bounces would bounce the same amount as the original bounce. Now, secondary bounces are always 2.
- Siege Attack now creates Scorch on ALL tiles.
- Siege Attack base damage 3=>4
- Siege Attack splash damage was 1-2, now is 1-3
- Knight Charge now breaks enemy armor (-2 armor).
- In Ranked/Custom games you now start with 1 fewer unit (chosen at random). There are also 3 rescues (up from 1) and one of them is guaranteed to be your faction's missing unit.
- Skelly Archer's Aimed Shot now does 2/5 damage, up from 1/4. Also there's a sound now for the arrow hitting.
- Max range of the Omni Catapult is now 3 (down from 4)
- Enemies moving in fog now move quickly, and make a subtler sound.
- Omni Unit Health changes: Longbow 8 => 6, Lich 10 => 8, Royal Guard 10=>8
- The Farmer's "Rake" ability is removed; instead, he now has the Turtlepult's launch ability, renamed Toss.
- The Turtlepult is now "Snapping Turtle", has new art, and no longer has Launch.
- Band Together now gives the defensive bonus to both involved units.

notes.title: 1.42, #TinyTeams stream, a new video, and a 20% off sale?!?!
notes.content:
If you missed it, I put out a video yesterday that should catch people up on the biggest updates that have happened in the six months since launch. You can watch that [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FmiVXotMRqM]HERE[/url]!

Also, GEM WIZARDS TACTICS is now ON SALE for 20% off, matching our biggest sale ever from about a month ago. This won't happen again anytime soon, so now's people's best chance to pick up the game. It's also, as you can see, in the best shape it's ever been in!

Finally, today (right now as I'm writing this) the #TinyTeams people are streaming, and they're going to stream Gem Wizards Tactics! YAY! Go check them out HERE: https://www.twitch.tv/yogscast

And now, onto the PATCH NOTES!

[h1]Version 1.42[/h1]
Welcome to version 1.42! This is a big version for balance changes, UI cleanup, and Campaign Mode. The changing of Gem Power from a resource you had to manage, to now being a single pickup that charges your cooldowns is the biggest change. And yes, the game is back to its original conception of having COOLDOWNS on abilities. This will help players at both the highest and lowest end of the skill spectrum: highest, because it makes the game harder at the highest level. Lowest, because there are effectively fewer decisions to make each turn. It's really good to have some *simpler* turns, I think! In addition to this we have a lot of improvements to Bill Milton's powers, most notably his new POLICIES which are very powerful one-time-use abilities. Enjoy!

- New PROGRESSION system.
- Total number of enemies decreased significantly.
- Most enemy units do not get level ups at all.
- "Gem Power" concept removed. Instead, all abilities have a 2 turn cooldown.
- Gems, when picked up, now refresh that unit's cooldowns, and heal the unit for 2 health.
- New VOLUNTEERS system in Campaign.
- Bill now has a new, cleaner system for his Portfolio. He collects "Million" buffs that he can spend on a new system called POLICIES instead. You now only get millions from collecting oil and giving out loans.
- Bill's BRIBE removed from the game.
- Bill has a new ability: Limo. He can teleport from any Road Tile to any visible Road Tile, and gain 1HP.
- Bill bugfix: Develop wasn't paving Rivers!
- Develop can now only target unoccupied tiles, BUT, will also *always* produce a gargoil. Much cleaner!
- Crippling Debt bonus damage 1 > 2
- Develop no longer creates extra oil on tiles.
- Earliest ranks in Custom and Ranked made even easier, in that they only require 1 or 2 flag captures.
- Knight charge range increased from 2-3 to 2-4.
- RESCUABLE position moved back to opposite center.
- Splashmasters now have the AQUATIC movement type.
- Splashmasters no longer require SPLASHBLASTER AMMO for the SPLASHBLASTER.
- The RANK system makes a lot more sense now. It is much simpler: units start with 0 stars. Each star increases your ATTACK by 1, to a max of 3.
- Caravan Upgrade: Gem Lab now gives +1AP upon picking up a gem.
- More improvements to UI and usability.
- The Map Editor isn't *quite* ready, but will be added in a version soon!

notes.title: 1.41 - UI overhaul, ultra-wide support, two new "factions" in custom mode, more!
notes.content:
This is yet another huge one! Look at all this stuff! We have a whole new, revamped, cleaned up UI that I'm pretty happy with. We have improvements to almost every part of gameplay. We have A LOT of improvements to the Neverending Party, our newest faction, who is getting closer to being up to snuff, design wise, with the Potatoes.

Oh, and there are two "new" pseudo-factions available for playing in Custom Games: the Omni-Mob (the enemies that you normally play against), and the Free Agents (units like the Vampire who don't have a faction). They're not balanced, but I figured - why not give people the option to play around with them anyway!

We now are also supporting some 21:9 Ultra-wide screen resolutions, which a few of you have been asking for.

And as always, a ton of bug fixes and polish stuff. One of my favorite new features is coded by one of our lead players who has now become a part time volunteer coder on the game, Reschiiv! He has put in a feature that puts KEYWORDS such as BUMPED or NEVERENDING automatically in a nice blue, bold font. This should really help communicate these things to players. Not only that but Reschiiv also put in a new feature that lets you see related BUFF tooltips when you hold CTRL while hovering a skill.

Stay tuned, because there is a VERY BIG DEAL new feature coming in the next patch!

UI/APP

- We now support several 21:9 (Ultra-Wide) screen resolutions!

BUSINESS DEMONS

AZURE ORDER

THE POTATOES

THE NEVERENDING PARTY

BUGFIXES
- Removed some text that referred to "Supplies" when your wizard

- Another fix to health bar UI.
- Fixed a bug where flags would get collected more than once.

- Several fixes to Deathberry Bushes not spawning when they should

notes.title: 1.40 - another huge one! Improvements in every area of the game!
notes.content:
Literally every part of the game has been improved for this one. Significant improvements to polish, balancing, bugfixing, difficulty, and more. The game is now cleaner and easier to get "onboarded" onto than ever before, with changes like "no half-AP ever" and the "slow start" for Campaigns. The game is easier at the easy-end, and harder at the harder end. The Business Demons and the Neverending Party in particular have gotten big upgrades with this patch, with both of their kits becoming more interesting and viable.

I'm excited to hear how the HILL tiletype changes how people play. This, plus reducing the Omni-mob health values, is an attempt to make "attacking" a bit more viable as part of your strategic kit. The Fire Mage and the pyro desperately needed a little love, so I put "melt armor" into the Fireball and Flamethrower skills, and gave the Fire Mage a completely new ability. Excited to see how that goes!

I have two more Business Demon changes planned for the future, but they're in a better spot than ever now. Enjoy!

[b]Version 1.40[/b]
CAMPAIGN MODE
- Campaign Mode now starts you with just four units, which will help new players onboarding but also will create more of an RPG power growth curve to the game.

DIFFICULTY
- There are now a unique number of flags required for each mission at each campaign difficulty level. This will make 
the difference between each campaign much more significant!
- Apprentice difficulty made even easier.

TERRAIN
We've gotten rid of the pesky .5 movement cost stuff again. It wasn't really pulling its weight, and it lead to a lot of annoying situations where you couldn't use an ability because you only had .5 AP left.
- Forest move cost reverted to 1
- New tile-type: Hill! +2 Attack. Appears on all maps except Desert.
- Bunny Builder Bridge movement cost 0.5 > 1

THE OMNIMOB
Tweaked some health of enemy units a bit, to make attacking a bit more valuable overall.
- Omni Drill Sgt. Health 10 > 8
- Omni Reaper health 10 > 8
- Omni Fire Mage Health 10 > 8
- Omni Ice Mage health 8 > 6
- Omni Fire Mage now only has fireball
- Omni Fire Mage is now fire-immune

The Gem economy for this faction was all messed up, and Riot wasn't really working as a good part of the faction's kit.

- Eve "Riot" Skill GP cost 4 > 3. Range reduced by 1, and now gives +1 AP.
- Death Bolt cost 1 > 0
- Gaze of Terror cost 0 > 1

BUSINESS DEMON IMPROVEMENTS
- Fire Mage Fireball Melt Armor ability removed.
- Fire Mage has a new ability: Wildfire. Within 2 tiles, all flames spread to adjacent tiles that contain an enemy, dealing 2 Fire Damage.
- Fire Mage Fireball ability now applies the Melt Armor Buff.

- Flamethrower now hits 3 tiles, dealing 3 damage to the first tile hit and 1 to the rest. Also applies 
- Bill's Debt buff now gives +1 Attack (no defense loss). Fixed tooltip.

BUGFIXES
- Re-wrote the code for the moves-left indicator, which wasn't working properly before.
- Fixed a bug where the Omni Golem was casting spells on the enemy team
- Fixed a bug where the RESTART button was missing from the Escape menu for Custom games.
- Flames had been damaging units twice as much as they should have. Flames now only hit you at the end of your turn (this goes for enemies too), or when you step into them.
- Fixed an issue where units who had > 10 HP's actions were getting covered up by health.

MISC

- You can now use right click to drag the camera.
- Knight's Charge ability now stops *before* forests (now more similar to Reaper Pull)

notes.title: Version 1.36: NEW and IMPROVED rules for bumping, bug fixes and more!
notes.content:
[b]Version 1.36[/b]
This version includes a pretty intense reworking, both code wise and rules wise of the BUMPING rules. They're something I've been working on and trying to get just right for awhile. Thanks to everyone in the Discord and the Steam forums for your help on this issue. Here's the new rules as listed in the Help screen: 
BUMPING is moving a unit forcefully. You can always BUMP a unit, unless there is a "SUPER HEAVY" (I'm going to rename this "immovable" later) unit behind them. If they move at least 1 full tile before hitting another unit, they'll deal damage based on how far they slid before they did. If units are adjacent to each other in a line, BUMPING one of the units bumps them all, in a chain.

Overall this version is a pretty big deal I think, especially for new players trying to understand how abilities are supposed to work.

PATCH NOTES:
- "Chain Bumping" removed! All bumps are now chainbumps.
- Fixed some bugs with splashmaster not putting as much water down as you'd expect.

Gameplay in general now will be a bit more quick and to the point. Knowing when you'll have the AP to use your abilities just got WAY easier, because movement calculations are way simpler (all tile types cost 1 to move to, except river which costs 2). All abilities also cost 1 AP now. In general this should just "smooth out" the experience.

Probably the biggest change is the addition of the OMNI-MOB, a sort-of-new-faction of AI-only monsters. They're recolored versions of units like the Royal Guard, the Spudling, and several others, hand-picked to be "good as AI-controlled units". They also now are greatly simplified - no longer do they have all the same abilities as the player even though they could never know how to use Bulldoze or Chill Step properly - and have more specific amounts of health than before that helps me set up the challenge in a more fluid way.

notes.title: State of the Game for April 2021
notes.content:
It is an interesting thing to be in a state of rapid flux, but also to be simultaneously in a state of feeling quite good about the game.

In the first month since launching the game, we* were primarily focused on improving the quality of the [i]app [/i]- by that, I mean that we've been adding more modes and expanding on the various modes that are already there. Over time, and more so recently, we've been focusing on improving the basic gameplay of Ranked/Campaign Modes, which I consider to be the "core" of [i]Gem Wizards Tactics[/i].

One of the tricky things to get right is, as always, "difficulty". I'm dealing with the highest ranked players the game has largely, and so I am very focused on the higher end of play recently and making sure it works. While it is true that you don't want to take the high-level feedback as any kind of gospel, given that often games change in how they're played at the highest level, it is also true that sometimes high level play can expose problems that are actually operational at all levels.

Something I've had my eye on is the idea of "playing defensively". In particular, I've been wanting to address two problems for awhile, that I've seen at all levels of play:
[list]
[*] The propensity to play [b]too defensively[/b]; to sit in one area and wait for enemies to come to you, or to move up way too slowly.
[*] Somewhat related, the fact that there's no rush to take towers; once you've cleared a tower, it kind of makes sense to sit on it for awhile until you've really secured the area or possibly until you can win.
[/list]

These kinds of gameplay dynamics have always been things I've cared about. Today I'm going to write real quick about three things that I'm doing to improve the basic gameplay of the game.

[b]GEMS[/b]
This game has "gems", which are around the map and which need to be collected so that you can use your more powerful abilities. The basic idea here is, you must keep moving in order to stay "fully powered"; if you just sit back and turtle, you'll quickly run out of gems and be unable to fight as effectively. Gems also are cool in that they change "tile valuation" in a randomized way - normally I'd want to move to 5,5 in this situation but there's a gem at 5,6 so maybe I'll move there - that sort of thing.

On a basic level, gems are doing that job. But a change we made last month has thrown a bit of a monkey wrench into that dynamic: specifically, the change that gives you +1 gem for killing a unit. What this has done is it has made "killing units" even more valuable, thereby massively increasing the value of "insta-kill" abilities (mainly, those that knock units off the map), but also, it has made turtling more possible. Exacerbating this problem has been my desire to "crank up the difficulty" in general for the highest ranks, which lead to me adding too many units to the game. I'll get back to this in the Sand Golem section.

Anyways, my new solution is this: we increase all the Gem values by double. Spells GP cost is basically doubled, with a few exceptions (some spells that were 1GP will stay 1GP, or some spells that were 2GP become 3GP, etc). This gives us a little bit more resolution with the spells as you can see, which is nice.

But also, we can make enemy unit kills worth only 1, thereby making it much more valuable to go out there and collect gems after all. 

It's been tough to find that middle ground, where when you hit 0 GP, you're not totally powerless, but you are definitely powered down. I'm hoping that this will not only help us balance the gem economy, but also the strategy space and even help us fine tune some abilities Gem costs. 


[b]FLAGS[/b]
You may remember that we recently added ICON-FLAGS in version 1.06 (feels like ages ago, actually). The whole idea there was that there wasn't any in-match reason to capture a flag, so players would kind of just sit on the flags. Having these specific ICON-FLAGS that gave you a particular benefit helped somewhat to get players thinking strategically about flags, but I think they didn't go nearly far enough.

So now we're doing this:
1. ALL flags, when you capture them, heal your entire squad by 5 (!!!) AND delays enemy reinforcements by a turn. This is such a massive change, and yet, I feel like it will work (in early testing it seems cool, although the game has gotten a lot easier.)
2. The "Heart" flag, which used to heal that single unit to full, has been replaced, given that it wouldn't make much sense anymore. Instead it is replaced by the EARTHQUAKE FLAG, which damages nearby enemy units and stuns them. To me this feels a lot more like a thing you can "go for" in a kind of rushy way, especially when combined with #1.
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38602491/c6e1b6989ae9a32d53fe2493ff339a86c23b0066.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38602491/1adb1dc05d8b4f58c454463f1f86d2892343322b.png[/img][/url]
3. We're removing Rest from the game completely. I've been wanting to do this for awhile. It's kind of an old wargame thing, it's somewhat ham-fisted and a lot of players don't even realize you can do it.


[b]THE SAND GOLEM[/b]
So as I said, a lot of this has made the game easier. Which it is, and which I'll continue working on going forward. But part, maybe a big part of the challenge with 1.24 on will be dealing with the SAND GOLEM.

Every 5 turns, a Sand Golem spawns in the middle of your starting area. Sand Golems cannot be damaged. Sand Golems cannot be be bumped, or bounced. Sand Golems have a 7 damage ability that knocks a unit back.

That's a lot of bad news for the players. They only have 3AP, so as long as you keep moving, you should be alright. My goal is for Sand Golems to really only affect players who are really playing slowly - but we'll keep an eye on it, maybe they need to have 2AP or some other restriction.

All in all, I'm really excited about these changes.

Oh, and we also do have another whole faction coming soon... more on that later!

Thanks for reading!!


*By the way, I am a solo indie dev company, but I say "we" because the truth is that I couldn't be doing what I'm doing without the help of my amazing kbgames community: Bowles, Reschiiv, Brett Lowey, Holographic Doll, Tirean, GodsPlan, Nomorebirds and many others. I really couldn't do any of this stuff without you guys and I consider many of you to be deeply involved in the game design process, and thank you so much for your help!

notes.title: Version 1.20! The Caravan, and no more permadeath!
notes.content:
[i][b]Gem Wizards Tactics no longer has "permadeath"![/b][/i]

I've always had issues with the term "permadeath", actually, because it's kind of unclear, it's kind of mixing mechanical and narrative (what is "death" exactly?)

Anyway, as we were experimenting with the new CARAVAN mode on the Beta Branch, one of our top GWT testers and all around awesomeguy, [url=https://twitter.com/ryanbowles42]Ryan Bowles[/url] (he's making his own cool turn based game which you should check out!) suggested, what if we just got rid of permadeath completely and made it that units were just benched for 1 mission if they were killed?

At first I was kinda unsure about that. I mean, isn't the whole premise with a mode like this, that X-Com style "gaining and losing guys" economy? But at the same time, for a long time I had been bugged by the fact that gameplay in Ranked Mode was strategically very different from that in Campaign Mode. In Ranked Mode, it's perfectly reasonable to make sacrifice plays, where you lose a unit to achieve some objective. In Campaign Mode, you couldn't do that nearly as much.

Then, when we added the "hit points are saved between missions" in the first Beta version of the Caravan, another playtester Reschiiiv noticed that now the game had become extremely calculationy and intense. Every single hit point mattered now. Maybe that's not super good for a game that is trying to be [url=http://keithburgun.net/how-to-add-strategy-to-your-tactics-game/]more strategic and less tactical[/url].

So, with all this in mind, and with Ryan's awesome suggestion, I decided to go completely the other way and get rid of Permadeath completely. Now, when a unit dies in battle, it's simply benched for 1 mission. (Your Wizard is still exempt from this, of course). There's no saving of hit points at all.

There will probably need to be other balance changes going forward; if anything, the game should be a bit easier now than it was before, at all levels. So I'm looking forward to your thoughts.

Without any further adieu, here are the patch notes - which also have many, many other significant changes! Check it out!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38602491/8643dcf507db66c3444d21fcdf5e57015d162405.png[/img]
[i]Above: a VERY early screenshot of the caravan mode, just to give you a sense.[/i]

During missions, there are treasure chests around the map, and once in awhile a unit, upon dying, drops a treasure chest. You can pick them up by walking over them. After the battle, your CARAVAN inventory will show all the treasure chests you picked up. Inside the treasure chests could be: 

- A random blessing
- Gold
- A random unit
- Any combination of these
- (later on) other stuff?

From there you can equip or sell blessings as you please to units in your squad. There will be a new little icon on units that have a blessing so you can easily see who has what.

But that's not all! There is also an UPGRADES menu, featuring four permanent upgrades that you can unlock for this campaign: Beds (oh I forgot to mention, units now only heal a little bit between missions. But beds mean units that don't go on missions heal to FULL), Surgery (one random unit who dies on a mission actually survives with 5 health), Gem Lab (Start each mission with extra gems) and Training (units not brought on a mission increase in level, capped at level 3). These each cost a decent chunk of Gold so it's a bit of a longer term power curve.

I'm really excited for this mode and looking forward to getting more feedback on it. I'm hoping to have it ready sometime around this coming weekend, but we'll see how it goes.

Thanks so much for checking out this update!

notes.title: Version 1.06

This is a really exciting one! We've been getting a lot of feedback about the game and hopefully this shows that we're taking it to heart. Now only do we have the new difficulty modes in Campaign Mode now, but in Unranked Play you can actually modify the rate at which new squads spawn in (or even turn it off completely!). This should give more players the ability to play the game how they want.

What I'm personally most excited about is the Icon-flags system. I really think it's a big bump in how strategic (as opposed to tactical) the game is, and that's exciting.

Also: BEWARE! The AI is a lot smarter now. Well, not really - it's more just that they were unnecessarily ending their turn after using a spell before. Now, they don't!

There's a ton of other cool stuff in here, polish, balance, bugfixing and pretty much everything else you could imagine. I'm really excited, maybe I'll do some streaming myself tomorrow. Come on by! (www.twitch.tv/keithburgun).
